panels.text: Nineveh, capital of Assyria, 7th century BCE. The Royal Library of Ashurbanipal is named after Ashurbanipal, the last great king of the Assyrian Empire.
It is a collection of more than 30,000 clay tablets and fragments, with texts of all kinds and in various languages. Among its holdings was the famous Epic of Gilgamesh.

Late 1849: the first discovery is made in the South-West Palace, the Royal Palace of king Sennacherib. The materials were found at Kouyunjik, in northern Mesopotamia. The discovery is credited to Austen Henry Layard.
Most of the tablets were taken to England and can now be found in the British Museum. The site is in modern-day northern Iraq, within the city of Mosul.
